title: One human family (Nostra Aetate 1)
hook: all peoples are one community with one origin and one final goal
tomorrow: can anyone ever be forced to find God?

segments.voice: Last week ended on the gift of self: found by giving. Gaudium et Spes said God wants all people to be one family. Today another council document starts right there.

Two seven-year-olds on a playground bench, best friends from two different faiths, are mid-argument, the way kids argue. My God made the whole world. No, mine did. A grown-up walks over to break it up, and before she can say a word, one of them looks up and asks her straight out: so where did everybody come from? And where is everybody going? It's a kid's question. It's also the question a council of bishops chose for the opening of its document on other religions.
screen: `TWO BEST FRIENDS, TWO FAITHS.` → `WHERE DID EVERYBODY COME FROM?` → `AND WHERE IS EVERYBODY GOING?`

segments.voice: The document is Nostra Aetate, Latin for in our time, and its first paragraph leans on the word one. One community: all peoples, it says, are one community. One origin: God made the whole human race to live across the earth. That comes from Paul's speech in Athens, in Acts: God "hath made of one, all mankind, to dwell upon the whole face of the earth." One final goal: God, whose care and goodness and saving plan reach everyone. Then the paragraph turns to the questions people bring to their religions. What is a person? What is the meaning of life? What is good, and what is sin? Where does suffering come from? What's the road to real happiness? What about death, and judgment, and what comes after? And what is the final mystery that surrounds our lives, the one we come from and move toward? Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Church's document on other religions doesn't open with differences. It opens with a family: one origin, one goal, and the same questions asked across humanity. The differences come later in the document, named honestly. But they're named inside a family.
screen: `ONE COMMUNITY.` · `ONE ORIGIN: MADE OF ONE.` · `ONE GOAL: GOD.` · `THE SAME QUESTIONS, EVERYWHERE.` · then, large: `ONE FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper, or your notes app. Write the names of three people whose faith or way of life is different from yours, and next to each name write the same word: family. Then sit with the list, and if you pray, pray for each of them by name.
One human family. Nostra Aetate's starting point: all peoples, one origin, one final goal, God.
Your line: one family. Same origin, same questions, and room at the table for the differences. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1590 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: CAN ANYONE BE FORCED TO FIND GOD?`

Nostra Aetate.meaning: Vatican II's declaration on other religions; Latin for in our time

Athens.meaning: the Greek city where Paul spoke to philosophers, in Acts

Acts.meaning: the Acts of the Apostles, the New Testament book after the Gospels

Paul.meaning: the apostle whose travels and letters fill much of the New Testament
